**🔒 Security & Privacy** | **🟠 Major** | **🏗️ Heavy lift**

**Do not make global routing the implicit Bedrock default.**

If an installation restricts where prompts can be processed, `region_name` does not confine this global profile to that Region. AWS can route requests across commercial Regions, and prompts or results may be stored in destination Regions. AWS also states that a request fails if an SCP blocks any destination Region. Select a suitable geographic profile for the configured Region, or require an explicit choice of global routing. ([docs.aws.amazon.com](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/inference-profiles-support.html))

Thanks. I kept the global profile on purpose: it's the same default strands-agents uses for `BedrockModel` (`DEFAULT_BEDROCK_MODEL_ID = "global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6"` in strands-agents 1.61.1), and `create_bedrock_model` returns a strands `BedrockModel`. A geographic profile (`us.` / `eu.` / `apac.`) would fail for anyone whose region isn't in that geography, and the bare in-region model ID no longer works on demand for current Claude models. Deployments with data-residency limits can still pass a geographic profile or their own `model_id`. Happy to switch to a region-derived prefix if the maintainers prefer that.

@pcbeingused333 Thanks for clarifying. `create_bedrock_model` accepts an explicit `model_id`, so deployments can select a geographic profile when required. The wrapper does not promise that `region_name` confines processing to that Region.

Global routing still has data-residency implications, but those implications do not establish a defect in this intentional default. I withdraw the requirement to change it. No change is needed for this finding.
